title: Old Trafford: overview
d: Old Trafford in Manchester, England: capacity about 74,310, opened 1910.
definition: Old Trafford in Manchester, England: capacity about 74,310, opened 1910.
description: Old Trafford stands in Manchester, England: a 74,310-capacity venue opened in 1910, home to Manchester United. The Theatre of Dreams. Stadiums are the cathedrals of sport — concrete memory banks where generations experienced the same joys and heartbreaks. This database covers the ground's history, architecture, great events, and how to visit it.

title: History
d: Old Trafford opened in 1910. The Theatre of Dreams..
definition: Old Trafford opened in 1910. The Theatre of Dreams..
description: The history of Old Trafford begins in 1910. The Theatre of Dreams. Like all great grounds, it has been rebuilt, renamed, and reborn — stands rising where terraces stood, roofs arriving decades after the first kick. Its timeline is the timeline of its tenants' triumphs and the city's love affair with the game.

title: Architecture
d: Old Trafford holds about 74,310 spectators in its current configuration.
definition: Old Trafford holds about 74,310 spectators in its current configuration.
description: The architecture of Old Trafford: a 74,310-capacity bowl designed to trap noise and frame the action. Great stadium design balances sightlines, acoustics, and atmosphere — the steepest stands feel closest, the roofs hold the roar in. Renovations keep adding hospitality while trying not to dilute the soul.

title: The tenants
d: Old Trafford is home to Manchester United.
definition: Old Trafford is home to Manchester United.
description: Old Trafford belongs to Manchester United — and to the fans who fill it. The tenant-club bond defines the ground's identity: the songs, the rituals, the expectation. When the team thrives the stadium shakes; when it struggles the old ground groans with it. You cannot separate the venue from its people.

title: Great matches
d: The greatest nights at Old Trafford live in legend.
definition: The greatest nights at Old Trafford live in legend.
description: The great nights at Old Trafford: title deciders, cup finals, impossible comebacks — the matches fans describe decades later as if they were yesterday. The Theatre of Dreams. Every old ground has a canon of such nights, and they are why the place matters: the stadium is the stage, but the drama is the point.

title: Finals hosted
d: Old Trafford has hosted major finals and showpiece events.
definition: Old Trafford has hosted major finals and showpiece events.
description: Showpiece events at Old Trafford: cup finals, international tournaments, and one-off spectacles that put the ground on the world stage. Hosting a final is a civic honor — the city dresses up, the world watches, and the stadium joins the short list of venues that have seen it all.

title: Concerts and events
d: Old Trafford doubles as a concert and event venue.
definition: Old Trafford doubles as a concert and event venue.
description: Beyond sport, Old Trafford hosts concerts, ceremonies, and mega-events — the biggest stages need the biggest rooms. The ground's event history reads like pop culture itself. Multi-use keeps the economics working, though purists always prefer the roar of a matchday to anything else.

title: Visiting guide
d: Visit Old Trafford: tours, matchdays, and practical tips.
definition: Visit Old Trafford: tours, matchdays, and practical tips.
description: Visiting Old Trafford: stadium tours run most days, taking in the dressing rooms, the tunnel, and the dugout — book ahead in season. On matchdays arrive early, learn the songs, and respect the home ends. Manchester, England is best reached by public transport; driving on event days is for the patient.

title: Best seats
d: Where to sit at Old Trafford for atmosphere, view, or value.
definition: Where to sit at Old Trafford for atmosphere, view, or value.
description: Seats at Old Trafford: behind the goal for the songs, halfway up the side for the tactical view, high corners for value. The famous ends have waiting lists measured in years; the family sections trade noise for comfort. Wherever you sit, the rule is the same — arrive early, stay late.

title: Attendance records
d: Old Trafford's biggest crowds and what drew them.
definition: Old Trafford's biggest crowds and what drew them.
description: The biggest crowds at Old Trafford came for the biggest occasions — derbies, finals, and farewell games. The Theatre of Dreams. Capacity has changed with all-seater conversions and expansions, so records from different eras are not directly comparable. What endures is the noise: full houses here are famously loud.

title: Fan culture
d: The songs and rituals of Old Trafford.
definition: The songs and rituals of Old Trafford.
description: Fan culture at Old Trafford: the anthems sung before kickoff, the scarves held high, the rituals passed down generations. Manchester United Every ground has its liturgy, and newcomers are expected to learn it. The culture is the point — the match is just the excuse for twenty thousand people to feel one thing together.

title: Derbies
d: Derby days at Old Trafford are the season's peak.
definition: Derby days at Old Trafford are the season's peak.
description: Derby days at Old Trafford divide the city: colors everywhere, nerves from dawn, and an atmosphere that visiting players never forget. Form goes out the window; pride decides it. Manchester United Win the derby and the season is saved — lose it, and the bragging rights belong to the other half of Manchester.

title: The future
d: What is next for Old Trafford.
definition: What is next for Old Trafford.
description: The future of Old Trafford: expansions, technology, and the eternal debate — renovate or relocate. Clubs outgrow grounds or grounds outlive clubs' ambitions; either way the fans' attachment complicates every decision. Whatever comes, the memories made here are permanent.
